summary: Publish-PR CI reconciliation: MCP main keeps the library-owned hardcoded version literal (no var version), account.go registers novel commands via direct cmd.AddCommand, and comments sweep routes every fetch through a testable sweepBudget gate that also halts on a server-side overcharge.
reason: Three library-side gates rejected the fresh 4.30.1 print shape. (1) The generator emits 'var version = ...' in cmd/<cli>-pp-mcp/main.go, but the public library's release-ledger workflow owns runtime version stamping; the base tree hardcodes the literal in server.NewMCPServer and the Verify guard blocks any change to it. (2) The generator attaches novel commands with addNovelCommandIfAbsent(...), which the library's verify_skill.py command-tree parser does not recognize (it matches only .AddCommand(newXxxCmd()), so account estimate/budget flags in SKILL.md/README hard-fail CI; direct cmd.AddCommand is what the previously published tree used. (3) Greptile P1: the sweep could spend past --max-credits. Every fetch — the initial posts fetch included — now passes one sweepBudget gate that admits a request only when the charged total plus the worst-case estimate (the running MAXIMUM per-fetch charge observed in the run, floor 1) stays within budget, so neither an ungated first request nor a stale last-charge estimate can let a costlier request through. Because per-request price is server-side and known only post-response, sweepBudget.charge additionally halts the sweep the moment a fetch takes the total past the budget, so an overshoot cannot compound; credits_charged always reports the true total. The gate is a standalone type pinned by amend_sweep_budget_test.go. All three must survive future reprints until fixed upstream in cli-printing-press. Upstream issues: #4040 (library verifier vs addNovelCommandIfAbsent), #4042 (MCP version stamping deadlock).
validated_outcome: verify_skill.py all checks pass; version-declaration diff vs library main empty; 6 sweepBudget unit tests pin first-fetch gating, running-max estimate, worst-case admission, overcharge halt, no-budget passthrough, and stop-note content; go build/vet/test green on both trees.
